prompt: Use case: illustration-story / identity-preserving animation key poses. Make a production sprite atlas for an offline children's learning app. Polished friendly storybook animal illustration with soft shaded fur/feathers/scales, clear anatomy and expressive eyes, matching the reference style. ONE animal identity reused in ALL cells, camera/head size/body proportions/markings EXACTLY consistent. Every pose is full body, no cropped limbs. All face RIGHT unless subject says front-facing. Genuine transparent background, NO coloured paper/background, floor, panels, labels, letters, numbers, arrows, speech bubbles, motion lines, cast shadows or decorative objects. Equal square grid cells with 8% safe margins, consistent scale, same notional ground baseline 85% down each cell for grounded poses. The top LEFT cell is frame1 and order is row-major. Carefully articulate actual jaws/legs/wings/tails; do NOT simply rotate/scale the entire animal as a substitute.  Layout: 4 columns, 2 rows, 8 poses. Each cell SQUARE. Overall atlas aspect ratio 4:2; exactly one full animal per cell with safe margins. All gaps and outside pixels alpha ZERO, true transparent cutouts. Input reference STYLE ONLY, NOT rabbit anatomy or colours. A friendly full-body grey elephant with big ears, pale small tusks, exactly four legs and one long trunk. Frames1–4 TRUNK USE: planted body, trunk reaching forward RIGHT and down, tip curling around a small brown branch, trunk raises the same branch, trunk lowers to place it down. Frames5–8 STOMP: same elephant, one forefoot planted and other raised clearly, raised forefoot higher with weight supported by other three legs, firm lowered/ground-contact pose, settled stance. Body scale fixed, no whole-body bounce, no water spraying.
